clips.text: Two moves today, both about saying something true out loud instead of keeping it to yourself: a genuine compliment, and a calm complaint. Both work better specific than vague.
¿Todo bien con la comida?
This is your opening. Está buenísimo works, but naming the actual dish gets a bigger reaction — it proves you weren't just being polite.
The food was genuinely excellent. Say so, specifically. Speak now.
El mole está buenísimo.
Muchas gracias, se lo voy a decir.
Now the other move. Something's actually wrong — not a preference, an actual problem. Name the object and the issue, calmly, without a speech attached.
The soup arrived cold. Name the problem, calmly. Speak now.
Disculpe, la sopa está fría.
Perdón, se la cambio ahora mismo.
Disculpe opens it without blame. Naming the object and the exact problem — not a general complaint — is what actually gets it fixed fast.
They fixed it fast. Thank them for taking care of it. Speak now.
Gracias por resolverlo tan rápido.
El mole está buenísimo. Disculpe, la sopa está fría. Gracias por resolverlo tan rápido.

I07 complete. A specific compliment brings the cook out to say thanks in person. A calm, specific complaint — disculpe plus the exact problem — gets it fixed fast, no confrontation required. Both moves work because they're honest and precise, not because they're loud.
